brief:
A documentary examining Israel's surveillance of Palestinian civilians in Gaza has attracted over 1.5 million viewers in less than two months, The Guardian reported. The film, titled NAZA and award-winning, details mass killings of civilians during the conflict.

The rapid viewership makes the documentary among the year's most watched releases. The project focuses on Israeli surveillance practices targeting Palestinians in the Gaza Strip.
